title: Corporate Governance Policies - Securities Trading Policy

tiers.name: directors, officers and employees
tiers.description: All directors, officers and employees of the Company and its related entities, and where appropriate contractors and consultants. Subject to the basic insider trading restrictions and the absolute ban on hedging unvested shares, options or rights under the employee equity scheme, but not to the closed periods or pre-trade notification regime.

tiers.name: Restricted Persons
tiers.description: Directors of the Company, all key management personnel as defined in AASB 124, and any other employees, contractors or consultants considered appropriate by the Managing Director and Company Secretary from time to time. Subject to the closed periods, the requirement to notify the Chairman and be advised there is no reason to preclude trading, the short-term trading ban and any Board embargo.

tiers.name: directors
tiers.description: Directors of the Company and any of their associates. Restricted Persons who must additionally notify the Company Secretary of any dealings within 5 business days, and who must immediately notify the Chairman or Company Secretary of the details of any hedging of vested options granted under the employee equity scheme.

tiers.name: key management personnel
tiers.description: Key management personnel as defined in Australian Accounting Standard AASB 124: Related Party Disclosure. Restricted Persons; a senior executive who hedges vested options must immediately notify the Chairman or Company Secretary of the details.

tiers.name: associated parties
tiers.description: Immediate family (including a spouse or equivalent or a dependent), family company or trust. Each Restricted Person is personally responsible for ensuring associated parties comply with the same restrictions, and the Board may embargo their trading.

definitions.hedging_definition: arrangements for the hedging, or otherwise limiting their exposure to risk in relation to unvested shares, options or rights issued or acquired under the Company's employee equity scheme

ad_hoc_blackout_authority: The Board has an absolute discretion to place an embargo on Restricted Persons and/or employees and/or their respective associated parties trading in Company securities at any time. The Policy does not say whether an embargo is confidential. Separately, the Chairman may impose conditions on any clearance, including time limits.

rules.section: General - Securities issued under equity-based remuneration scheme
rules.detail: Derivatives are not defined and the Policy does not otherwise regulate options or other financial products over Company securities. The only express treatment is that a director or senior executive who enters into arrangements for the hedging of vested options under the employee equity scheme must immediately notify the details to the Chairman or Company Secretary. A put and call over vested holdings is therefore not prohibited, but is subject to that notification and, where it involves a trade in the Company's securities, to the closed periods and the pre-trade Chairman notification process.
rules.evidence: Where a director or senior executive enters into arrangements for the hedging of vested options granted under the Company's employee equity scheme, details of the hedging arrangements must be immediately notified to the Chairman or Company Secretary.

rules.section: Requirements for trading by Restricted Persons
rules.detail: For a Restricted Person who is not a director or senior executive, nothing addresses derivatives over vested securities. The general obligation to notify the Chairman before trading, or giving instructions for trading, in the Company's securities and to await advice that there is no reason to preclude the trade would be applied to an arrangement of this kind, and the closed periods and any Board embargo would apply.
rules.evidence: Before trading, or giving instructions for trading in the Company's securities, a Restricted Person must: notify the Chairman ... of their intention to trade

rules.section: General - Securities issued under equity-based remuneration scheme
rules.detail: Any derivative or other arrangement limiting exposure to risk in relation to unvested shares, options or rights under the employee equity scheme is prohibited for everyone, with no approval or exceptional circumstances route.
rules.evidence: Directors, officers and employees of the Company are prohibited from entering into arrangements for the hedging, or otherwise limiting their exposure to risk in relation to unvested shares, options or rights issued or acquired under the Company's employee equity scheme.

rules.section: General - Securities issued under equity-based remuneration scheme
rules.detail: Absolute ban covering hedging and any other means of limiting exposure to risk in unvested plan shares, options or rights. It applies to all personnel, not only Restricted Persons, and there is no waiver power.
rules.evidence: Directors, officers and employees of the Company are prohibited from entering into arrangements for the hedging, or otherwise limiting their exposure to risk in relation to unvested shares, options or rights issued or acquired under the Company's employee equity scheme.

rules.section: General - Securities issued under equity-based remuneration scheme
rules.detail: Hedging of vested holdings is permitted. The only express obligation is immediate notification of the details of the hedging arrangements to the Chairman or Company Secretary; no prior approval of the hedge itself is required by that clause, although the pre-trade notification requirement and closed periods apply to any accompanying trade in the underlying securities. The clause is drafted around 'vested options granted under the Company's employee equity scheme' and does not expressly address hedging of ordinary shares held outright.
rules.evidence: Where a director or senior executive enters into arrangements for the hedging of vested options granted under the Company's employee equity scheme, details of the hedging arrangements must be immediately notified to the Chairman or Company Secretary.

rules.section: General - Securities issued under equity-based remuneration scheme
rules.detail: Same regime as directors for a senior executive: hedging of vested options is permitted subject to immediate notification of details to the Chairman or Company Secretary, and the closed periods, Board embargo and pre-trade Chairman notification apply to related trading in the underlying.
rules.evidence: Where a director or senior executive enters into arrangements for the hedging of vested options granted under the Company's employee equity scheme, details of the hedging arrangements must be immediately notified to the Chairman or Company Secretary.

rules.section: General; Requirements for trading by Restricted Persons
rules.detail: For a Restricted Person who is neither a director nor a senior executive the notification clause does not apply, and hedging vested holdings is not prohibited. The general pre-trade requirement to notify the Chairman of an intention to trade, confirm the absence of price sensitive information and obtain advice that there is no reason to preclude the trade is the applicable control.
rules.evidence: have been advised by the Chairman that there is no reason to preclude them from trading in the Company's securities as notified

rules.section: Requirements for trading by Restricted Persons; General
rules.detail: Monetisation structures are not named. A prepaid forward or collar-plus-loan over vested securities is not prohibited, but limiting exposure to risk in unvested plan securities is banned outright, and any element amounting to trading or giving instructions to trade in the Company's securities requires prior Chairman notification and clearance outside the closed periods.
rules.evidence: Before trading, or giving instructions for trading in the Company's securities, a Restricted Person must: notify the Chairman (or in the case of the Chairman intending to trade, notify the chair of the Audit Committee) of their intention to trade

rules.detail: Short selling is nowhere mentioned. A short position closed within one to six months would fall within the short-term trading prohibition for Restricted Persons, but the Policy contains no short selling rule.

Securities lending is not mentioned anywhere and there is no definition of trading or dealing that would sweep it in; a lend and return would arguably fall within the exclusion for transfers resulting in no change in beneficial ownership.

CFDs are not mentioned. A CFD over unvested plan securities would be an arrangement limiting exposure to risk and so prohibited; otherwise the Policy is silent, subject to the short-term trading ban on Restricted Persons.

rules.section: Trading circumstances excluded from share trading policy
rules.detail: There is no prohibition on, or approval or disclosure requirement for, entering into a margin loan over Company securities. Margin lending appears only as an example in the carve-out that takes a secured lender's enforcement sale outside the Policy.
rules.evidence: a disposal of securities that is a result of a secured lender exercising its rights, for example, under a margin loan arrangement.

rules.detail: Granting security, a charge or a pledge over Company securities is not mentioned and there is no definition of trading that would catch it; the Policy regulates trading and hedging only.

rules.section: Trading circumstances excluded from share trading policy
rules.detail: Secured financing over Company securities is neither prohibited nor made subject to approval or notification. The Policy positively assumes such arrangements may exist by excluding a secured lender's enforcement sale from its operation, so a loan secured on collared shares is unregulated by the Policy, though a director's dealings must still be notified to the Company Secretary within 5 business days.
rules.evidence: a disposal of securities that is a result of a secured lender exercising its rights, for example, under a margin loan arrangement.

rules.detail: Restricted Persons are generally prohibited from short-term trading at all times, defined as a purchase and sale of the same securities within a period between one and six months. No carve-out is stated for plan securities. Entry into and unwind of a collar, or a purchase to close followed by a sale, within six months is exposed to this restriction to the extent it involves the same securities.
rules.evidence: In order to prevent the unfair use of information, Restricted Persons are generally prohibited from short-term trading at all times. Short-term trading is a purchase and sale of the same securities within a period between one to six months.

exemption_authority: The Chairman or Managing Director, together with at least one other non-executive director, may give clearance for a Restricted Person to sell (but not purchase) securities during a closed period in exceptional circumstances such as severe financial hardship or a court order, provided the person holds no unpublished price sensitive information and the disposal is the only reasonable course of action available. Permission must be evidenced in prior written communication. No exemption power exists over the ban on hedging unvested plan securities.

bespoke_clauses.topic: hedging of vested options is notification only
bespoke_clauses.clause: Where a director or senior executive enters into arrangements for the hedging of vested options granted under the Company's employee equity scheme, details of the hedging arrangements must be immediately notified to the Chairman or Company Secretary.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Hedging vested holdings is expressly contemplated and requires only immediate disclosure of details, not consent, so the derivative legs are achievable.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The Policy contains no margin lending, secured financing or encumbrance provision; the only reference is the exclusion of 'a disposal of securities that is a result of a secured lender exercising its rights, for example, under a margin loan arrangement'.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The loan secured on the collared shares is neither prohibited nor subject to approval or notification, and lender enforcement is expressly outside the Policy even in a closed period.

bespoke_clauses.clause: have been advised by the Chairman that there is no reason to preclude them from trading in the Company's securities as notified
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Clearance is a discretionary Chairman confirmation with no stated validity period, response time or revocation rule, so the bank should fix its own execution deadline in the term sheet.

bespoke_clauses.clause: have complied with any conditions on trading imposed by the Chairman (including, for example, any time limits applicable to the clearance).
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The Chairman can attach conditions, including volume or timing limits, that may cut across the hedge ratio or execution schedule agreed with the bank.

bespoke_clauses.clause: in the two weeks prior to the release of the Company's quarterly reports and for 1 business day after the release of the report
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: With two week quarterly and four week half and full year blackouts, open windows are short and irregular for a quarterly reporting miner, so entry and roll dates must be planned around them.

bespoke_clauses.clause: the Board has an absolute discretion to place an embargo on Restricted Persons and/or employees and/or their respective associated parties trading in Company securities at any time.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: An unqualified embargo can be imposed at any time and extends to family trusts and companies, so it can block collar entry, roll or physical settlement without notice.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Short-term trading is a purchase and sale of the same securities within a period between one to six months.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Collar tenor and any unwind or re-hedge involving the same securities should exceed six months, and there is no carve-out for plan share sales as there is in many policies.

bespoke_clauses.topic: closed period relief is sale only
bespoke_clauses.clause: In exceptional circumstances clearance may be given for a Restricted Person to sell (but not to purchase) securities when they would otherwise be prohibited from doing so
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A closed period unwind requiring a purchase, such as buying back a written call, cannot be cleared even for hardship.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Each Restricted Person has a personal responsibility to ensure that his or her associated parties (being immediate family (including a spouse (or equivalent) or dependent), family company or trust) complies with the same respective restrictions.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A collar or facility booked through a family company or trust attracts the same clearance and notification obligations as one in the executive's own name.

bespoke_clauses.clause: arrangements for the hedging of vested options granted under the Company's employee equity scheme
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The notification clause is drafted around vested plan options rather than ordinary shares, so the treatment of a collar over shares held outright rests on the general trading clearance rather than an express permission.

summary: A funded collar is workable for a Red 5 / Vault Minerals director or senior executive over vested holdings, and the financing leg is essentially unregulated by this policy. Hedging of vested options is expressly permitted subject only to immediate notification of the details to the Chairman or Company Secretary, while hedging or otherwise limiting exposure to risk in unvested shares, options or rights under the employee equity scheme is banned outright for all personnel with no waiver. There is no margin lending, encumbrance or secured financing provision at all, and a disposal resulting from a secured lender exercising its rights is expressly excluded from the Policy, so a loan secured on the collared shares can be entered and enforced without breaching it. The practical constraints are the pre-trade requirement for a Restricted Person to notify the Chairman and be advised there is no reason to preclude the trade (with any conditions the Chairman imposes, and no stated validity period), the two week quarterly and four week half and full year closed periods, the Board's absolute discretion to impose an embargo at any time, and the ban on Restricted Persons buying and selling the same securities within one to six months. Directors must also notify the Company Secretary of any dealing within 5 business days.
